title: Offer 'Rescan as administrator' after a finished whole-drive scan of a local drive that left folders unread
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: A 'Rescan as administrator' offer exists on the scan's ending: missing
The offer is shown only after a finished scan (not stopped, refused, root unreadable or failed): missing
The offer is shown only for a whole-drive root, not a folder: missing
The offer is not shown for network, mapped or UNC drives (local drive only): missing
The offer is shown only when the scan left folders unread: missing
Pressing it relaunches the app elevated through the UAC prompt and scans the same root: missing

subst-letter-invisible-to-linked-elevated-token: not measurable on any machine here: Whether EnableLinkedConnections=1 makes the limited token's SUBST letter visible to the elevated token [N-074]; The same result for a real interactive elevation (consent prompt, user's session) rather than LogonUserW pair impersonation from SYSTEM [N-075] -- needs first: The design needs a way to hand the elevated copy a root it can open, because a bare SUBST letter chosen in the limited session does not resolve there. Candidates: resolve the SUBST target with QueryDosDevice under the limited token before handoff, or re-check the root under the elevated token. Neither was tried here.

In the elevated copy, the finished whole-drive coverage line still says the unseen space includes 'anything else an ordinary account cannot list' (MainWindow.xaml.cs Coverage, PS-012 wording, frozen by a constraint). This design keeps it word for word in both copies. Should the elevated copy be allowed different words, which means lifting the PS-012 constraint for that copy?
Uncontested, with one designer: the button sits on the pickers' line, not on the ending beside the Unreadable tab. It is always in view, but it is further from the count that explains it.
Uncontested: a new RescanStatus line, not the existing RevealStatus line at the bottom. It costs a control, but it keeps the reveal status words that window cases read from mixing with the rescan's.
Uncontested: the original window stays open after a successful start. The person can compare the two scans, at the price of two scan stores in memory.

The press itself end to end (UAC prompt, elevated copy scanning the same root): cannot be driven unattended, and the engine treats a raised prompt as misuse. Start is proved through the injected start function; finish line 6 stays the person's check on a UAC-on PC.
A test of 'start another scan after an offered ending' (case 14): not material in the design; the reset is HideRescanOffer beside StartScan's other Hide* resets, left for code review.
A picture of the offered ending: the screen capture is black in this session. The report's inView and PickerPanel height keys are the layout evidence.
SeBackupPrivilege, an elevated helper, IPC and merging into the open scan: left out on purpose, as the design's over_engineering_flag says.

Editing MainWindow, WindowReport and Core.Native makes the person's network, C:\ and OneDrive proof runs stale under the project's staleness lists; Q-016 already orders them after E-005, E-006 and E-007.

RescanAsAdministrator.IsDriveRootShape restates Core's internal VolumeSpace.IsDriveRoot. Exposing one public shape test from Core would remove the second copy; this slice kept to the design's restatement.

UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange(workers: 4) failed in 3 of 4 full runs here, and CancellationTests and a cloud stall test fail under this PC's load with my classes excluded. It deserves its own look; this slice did not touch scanning.
Q-002 (outcome texts capped at 76 px) is still open; the offer sits on the pickers' line to stay out of it, so it does not need Q-002 answered.

The RescanStatus line is trimmed with a tooltip at the 560 px minimum width (about 60 px of room beside the three buttons); a later slice could move the started/declined line if that proves too short in use.

deviation: Start also refuses a root that is not a whole-drive shape (NotADriveLine, Windows never called), which the design did not say. Reason: the command line goes to an elevated copy, and lesson #914 asks for crafted roots; a root carrying a quote, --report or a second argument can never reach it. It costs one branch, tested with folders, shares, bare letters and injection-shaped roots.

deviation: The design's case 13 and the planted E005 scripts are replaced as accepted finding M1 says: the SL-008 script owns case 13 as its own short CreateProcess runs before the drive scan (740, timeout and no report are FAILED), the stopped-scan negative is dropped, and the combination rule is any FAILED > any INCONCLUSIVE. UNC-share report negatives are not run at exe level (no share can be made unattended); the Offers tests cover the \\server and \\?\UNC\ spellings.

deviation: The engine-appended SL-008 fitness block was rewritten, not kept as it came: the Verb pattern became the elevation API-family ban (m3), manifest bans were added over src/** and root Directory.Build.* (m4), a call-site entry and a hook entry were added (M2), and the call-site pattern tolerates whitespace and line breaks around the dot.

deviation: The button's text and tooltip are set in MainWindow's constructor from RescanAsAdministrator's constants rather than written in the XAML, so the words are written once and the linked tests see the same ones.
deviation: SettledRulesCorpusTests.Rule and ReadRule were made internal so the new corpus test reads fitness entries by the same reader instead of a second YAML reader.

deviation: No Settings checkbox or notice was built for the GLOBAL?? letter gate, as the design decided: Windows keeps a separate DOS-device map per logon session by design (it is documented, with EnableLinkedConnections as its own workaround), and the gate only withholds an offer that would end as 'Could not read'. I considered the standing one-checkbox-per-outside-defect rule against that decision and kept the design; a reviewer who reads it as an outside defect should say so.
